cl_alc_how_it_kills.q: How can you die from alcohol?
cl_alc_how_it_kills.short: Mostly through injuries, heart and blood-vessel disease, cancer and liver cirrhosis. One world model put 38 in 100 alcohol deaths down to injuries. Cirrhosis was 15 in 100.
cl_alc_how_it_kills.but: No paper we hold says what alcohol poisoning does to the body, when someone drinks far too much at once. And the model is an estimate, not a count.
how: One model looked at deaths around the world in 2004. It put about 2.5 million down to alcohol. Of every 100, about 27 were accidents such as road crashes, falls, drownings and poisonings. Another 11 were self-harm or violence.
Heart and blood-vessel disease made up 22 in 100, cancer 20 and liver cirrhosis 15. Brain and mental health conditions made up 5. Before age 60, the authors say, injuries mattered most.

Two reviews pass on other people's figures. About 1 to 4 in 100 hospital patients with the DTs die. The DTs are a sudden confusion in alcohol withdrawal. People with alcohol use disorders have high death rates, mainly through conditions such as liver cirrhosis or injury.

The model is an estimate, not a count. It has no margins of error, leans on studies done mostly in richer countries and leaves out infections. It has no figure for alcohol poisoning, and no paper we hold describes it.
cl_alc_how_it_kills.rate: One computer model for 2004, with no margins of error, built on studies of groups of people mostly in richer countries. The other figures are passed on by two reviews. No paper on alcohol poisoning is on file.

alcohol.statement: In one world model, liver disease was the top way alcohol killed.
alcohol.why: Injuries came first: about 38 in 100 deaths put down to alcohol, against 15 for liver cirrhosis. It's a model's estimate, not a count of deaths.

alcohol.statement: In one world model, about 1 in 5 deaths put down to alcohol were from cancer.
alcohol.why: Cancer made up about 20 in 100, just behind heart and blood-vessel disease at 22. It's a model's estimate for 2004, not a count of deaths.
